svg.text: Total section A-A
through the east and west mid-span buttresses, looking north
Footing 1800 x 250, underside at -1000 (frost depth
and bearing are guesses).
Printed wall 400, same pattern as the roof: two 80
inner layers, a 160 air zone, an 80 outer layer.
Solid base of the roof: over the first 300
(vertical) above the eave the 160 air zone is filled
with cast concrete between the printed layers, so
the 400 is solid; there is no ring beam.
Buttress 400 wide, 1000 from the inner face (600
beyond the wall); it rises to +2.50, flush with the
roof base.
Roof shell: 400 thick square to the slope at the
base (two 80 inner layers, a 160 air zone, an 80
outer layer), 320 at the crown; about 500 / 400
horizontally.
Crown opening 1000 clear; roof rises 6000 over 4500,
slope 53.1° (36.9° from the vertical).
Everything is 3D printed: mortar beads in 10 mm
layers (joints drawn every 100) form permanent
formwork. Where a member is solid (roof base,
buttress, footing) the printed shell is filled with
cast concrete, crossed hatch. Single hatch = printed
only.
from your sketches
assumed by me, to confirm
Notes
Layer pattern from your drawing; at the crown the second
inner layer ends, so the leaf is 80 there (assumed).
The cut runs through the mid-span buttresses; the north
wall with its door and window is seen beyond.
Faint grid on the back roof face and the north wall =
printed pieces in running bond, about 1500 wide, 800 high
on the roof and 440 on the wall (assumed sizes).
